open_obligations: Compare black-box/white-box access, security assumptions and attack goals.
Identify counterexamples before any shared canonical backdoor definition.
in.rationale: Both abstracts address hidden backdoors, but computational undetectability and inability to elicit a trigger are different properties.
in.scope: distinct cryptographic backdoor constructions and defender access models: the undetectable-backdoor abstract plants backdoors in classifiers (in any model using digital signature schemes, and in models trained with Random Fourier Features or in Random ReLU networks) with stated guarantees, while the unelicitable-backdoor abstract builds backdoors in transformer language models and confirms their properties in empirical investigations
